title: Characterization of Diagonalizable Groups
body_html:
Characterization of Diagonalizable Groups

For a linear algebraic group \(D\) over an algebraically closed field, the following conditions are equivalent:

  1. \(D\) is diagonalizable, i.e. is isomorphic to a closed subgroup of a diagonal torus.
  2. The coordinate algebra \(k[D]\) has a basis consisting of characters of \(D\).
  3. Every finite-dimensional rational representation of \(D\) is a direct sum of one-dimensional character spaces.
proof_html:
If \(D\subseteq \operatorname{GL}_n\) is diagonal, the coordinate functions on \(D\) are generated by restrictions of diagonal characters. These characters form a group, and the coordinate algebra decomposes into their weight spaces; in fact the nonzero weight spaces are one-dimensional.

A character basis of \(k[D]\) makes every comodule over \(k[D]\) split into weight spaces, because the coaction of a finite-dimensional representation involves only finitely many basis characters. This gives complete reducibility into one-dimensional representations.

Conversely, apply the representation criterion to a faithful finite-dimensional representation of \(D\). It decomposes as a direct sum of characters, so \(D\) embeds into the diagonal subgroup of \(\operatorname{GL}(V)\).
